report.source_text: The patient is a 40-year-old male with a history of diabetes mellitus and ethanol use who was struck by a motor vehicle while ambulating in the street. The patient presented several days after the accident with complaints of worsening back pain and difficulties on ambulation. A physical exam at the time of presentation to the Emergency Department (ED) revealed exquisite midline and sacral spinal tenderness with no significant paraspinal tenderness. The patient had subacute bruising throughout his lower extremities, torso, back, and face, with bilateral bruising over his infraorbital region (Figure 1). The patient had no saddle anesthesia or lower extremity numbness or tingling. The patient did exhibit weakness in both extremities secondary to pain; however, the range of motion was intact. CT spine showed a nondisplaced L2 vertebral body fracture (Figure 2). No acute surgical intervention was indicated as per the neurosurgical team, and the patient could be managed outpatient with a Thoracic-Lumbar-Sacral Orthosis (TLSO) brace and pain control with NSAIDs, Robaxin, and Gabapentin. Neurosurgery also recommended that the patient obtain MRI L-spine without contrast.

report.source_text: Six days after the initial presentation, the patient presented to the ED again with increasing back and left lower extremity pain, confusion, auditory hallucinations, and fever for three days. He was tachycardic to 109 bpm and febrile to 101-102F (38.8C). Neuromuscular examination demonstrated 2/5 strength in bilateral lower extremities. He was unable to perform hip flexion and leg elevation. Sensation was grossly intact throughout both lower extremities. He had a white blood cell count of 24,000/mcL with a lactate of 2.8 mmol/L. The patient was also found to be in diabetic ketoacidosis with a blood glucose of 588 mg/dL, an anion gap of 26, and a pH of 7.35. Subsequent imaging showed L2 paraspinal soft tissue mass with multilocular low attenuation changes in the left psoas muscle. At that time, there was concern for an infected hematoma or an intramuscular abscess.

clinician.trajectory_summary: 40-year-old male with diabetes mellitus and ethanol use was struck by a motor vehicle and presented to the ED several days later with worsening back pain and ambulatory difficulties. Initial CT spine showed a nondisplaced L2 vertebral body fracture with no acute surgical indication. Six days after initial ED presentation, the patient returned with fever, confusion, auditory hallucinations, tachycardia (109 bpm), and severe lower extremity weakness (2/5 strength). Laboratory evaluation revealed severe hyperglycemia (blood glucose 588 mg/dL), diabetic ketoacidosis (anion gap 26, pH 7.35), elevated WBC (24,000/mcL), and lactate of 2.8 mmol/L. Imaging at readmission demonstrated L2 paraspinal soft tissue mass with multilocular low attenuation changes in the left psoas muscle, concerning for infected hematoma or intramuscular abscess. MRI confirmed bilateral psoas abscesses with L2 fracture edema and L5-S1 disc protrusion. Interventional radiology drainage of the left psoas yielded 20 mL of purulent material positive for Methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA). Subsequent CT revealed a new left gluteal fluid collection with gas, requiring repeat IR drainage of left gluteal (20 ccs serosanguineous) and right psoas (4 ccs serosanguinous) collections with negative cultures. The patient received intravenous cefazolin therapy (vancomycin was discontinued) during a ten-week hospital stay, with eventual discharge showing complete alleviation of symptoms and only occasional mild lower back discomfort. Clinical improvement was documented with 4/5 lower extremity strength after drainage procedures.
